styleWhy: The story is a share and a growth rate (percentages, terawatt-hours, a share of new demand), so clean animated charts show the comparison better than any scene of a solar panel could.

copy.idea: Solar still makes only a small slice of the world's electricity, but it is growing more than any other source: up 30% in 2025, and it alone met three quarters of the rise in demand.
copy.hook: How much of the world's electricity comes from the Sun?
copy.body:
In 2025, solar made 8.7% of all the electricity the world generated: about 1 unit in every 11.

That is still small. Coal alone made a third, and gas more than a fifth.

But solar is the growth story. Its output rose 30% in one year, a record 636 TWh, to 2,778 TWh. Solar alone met 75% of the rise in the world's electricity demand.

For the fourth year running, solar grew more than any other source. Small slice, biggest growth.

facts.text: Solar generated 8.7% of global electricity in 2025, almost level with nuclear. Quote: "Solar reached 8.7% of global generation in 2025, almost matching nuclear's share (8.9%)". (About 1 in 11 is our arithmetic: 100 ÷ 8.7 ≈ 11.5.)
facts.source: Ember, World electricity data page (Global Electricity Review 2026 data) — https://ember-energy.org/countries-and-regions/world/

facts.text: Shares of global electricity in 2025: coal 33% ("Coal fell to 33%, dropping below one-third for the first time"), gas 21.8%, hydro 14% ("Hydro remains the largest individual source of low-carbon electricity at 14%"), nuclear 8.9%, wind 8.5% ("wind rose to 8.5%"), solar 8.7%. 'Other' (5.1%) is the remainder, our arithmetic.
facts.source: Ember, World electricity data page (Global Electricity Review 2026 data) — https://ember-energy.org/countries-and-regions/world/

facts.text: Solar generation grew 30% in 2025, adding a record 636 TWh. Quote: "Solar power increased by a record 636 TWh to reach 2,778 TWh in 2025, a 30% increase". (2024 ≈ 2,778 − 636 = 2,142 TWh is our arithmetic.)
facts.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026, published 21 April 2026 — https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/global-electricity-review-2026/

facts.text: Solar met three quarters of the growth in electricity demand in 2025. Quote: "Solar power alone met 75% of the net increase in electricity demand".
facts.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026, published 21 April 2026 — https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/global-electricity-review-2026/

facts.text: Solar had the largest absolute growth of any source for the fourth year in a row. Quote: "For the fourth year running, solar recorded the largest absolute growth of any electricity source."
facts.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026, published 21 April 2026 — https://ember-energy.org/latest-insights/global-electricity-review-2026/

shots.title: Hook: how much is solar?
shots.show: Rolling counter: a huge gold '0.0%' fills the middle of the navy frame and rolls up to 8.7%, landing with a bounce. Behind it a soft gold sun disc pulses; beneath it a thin full-width bar (the 'world electricity' bar of shot 2) fills just its first 8.7% in gold, the rest dim slate. Small label above: 'SHARE OF WORLD ELECTRICITY · 2025'. A row of 11 bolts, the first gold: ≈ 1 unit in every 11 (labelled arithmetic).
shots.motion: Counter rolls 0→8.7 in 1.6 s and bounces; the gold sliver wipes in with it; sun disc breathes; light rays rotate slowly behind the number.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 (8.7% of 2025 generation; 100 ÷ 8.7 ≈ 11.5 → ≈ 1 in 11, arithmetic)

shots.title: Still a small slice
shots.show: Split bar: the same world-electricity bar from shot 1, now tall and vertical down the frame, splits into labelled segments stacking from the top: coal 33%, gas 21.8%, hydro 14%, nuclear 8.9%, wind 8.5%, solar 8.7% (gold) at the bottom, plus a thin 'other' (5.1%, the remainder). Fossil segments in muted slate-red, clean sources in teal, solar in gold. Each segment's % counter rolls as it appears; the coal block is outlined so its size beside solar is obvious.
shots.motion: Segments slide in one after another from the top with rolling percentages; at the end the gold solar segment glows and ≈3.8 copies of it stack up beside the coal block.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 (shares of 2025 generation; coal 33% ÷ solar 8.7% ≈ 3.8)

shots.title: +30% in one year
shots.show: Two gold vertical bars side by side: 2024 (≈2,142 TWh) and 2025 (2,778 TWh). The 2025 bar grows past the 2024 bar; the extra slice on top is highlighted bright gold with a rolling '+636 TWh' label. A big '+30%' counter rolls at the top. Ground dots stream upward into the new slice like particles of energy.
shots.motion: 2024 bar rises first, then the 2025 bar grows and overshoots; the added slice fills with flowing particles while +30% and +636 TWh roll up.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 (2024 ≈ 2,778 − 636 = 2,142 TWh, arithmetic)

shots.title: Three-quarters of new demand
shots.show: The net rise in world electricity demand in 2025 stands as a column of four equal blocks labelled 'NET RISE IN DEMAND · 2025'. The bottom three fill gold one after another, each marked 25%; the top one stays dim slate, 'the rest'. Beside them a big gold '75%' rolls up over a soft sun disc, 'MET BY SOLAR ALONE' beneath it.
shots.motion: Empty blocks are set out from the first frame; gold drops into three of them in turn with a flash while bolts rise off the newest; the 75% counter rolls with the fills and lands with a bounce; a bracket draws along the gold blocks.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 ("Solar power alone met 75% of the net increase in electricity demand")

shots.title: Biggest growth, 4 years running
shots.show: Bar race: horizontal bars labelled 'Growth in generation' for 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, one row per year; in each row solar's gold bar races other sources (teal wind, slate others) and finishes first, a gold '#1' badge stamping on it. Four badges stack in a column on the right, then a '4 years running' tag.
shots.text: Biggest growth of any source, 4 years running
shots.motion: Rows race in turn, each about 0.75 s; gold bar overtakes and the #1 badge stamps; the four badges glow together at the end.
shots.source: Ember, Global Electricity Review 2026 (bar lengths illustrative; ranking from source)

shots.title: End card
shots.show: The world-electricity bar from shot 1 returns, gold sliver at 8.7%, and an upward gold arrow labelled '+30%' (solar output, 2025) pushes the sliver wider as the title sets above: 'Small slice. Biggest growth.' Source line at the foot.
shots.motion: Gold sliver creeps wider under the arrow; title types in; sun disc glows softly behind.

recurring.name: World electricity bar
recurring.design: One long bar standing for 100% of world electricity in 2025, rounded ends, dim slate fill; solar's 8.7% always gold and always at the same end (left when horizontal, bottom segment when the bar stands vertical in shot 2); clean sources teal, fossil sources muted slate-red; label 'WORLD ELECTRICITY · 2025' in small caps.

recurring.name: Solar gold
recurring.design: Solar is always warm gold (bars, counters, badges, sun disc); other clean sources teal; fossil fuels muted slate-red; never swapped.
